notes:
Summary: evaluation stalled, ultimately lost to cheaper vendor. Primary objection = unit economics (token + GPU cost) + required commit too large for current budget.

Highlights / quotes:
- Head of ML (S. Patel): "Redwood perf is excellent but we can’t justify 3x token spend vs competitor for embeddings at our scale."
- CTO: wants on-prem option but procurement balked at minimum commit.
- Security OK with SOC2 + SSO but needs formal data residency doc; that stalled timeline.

Pricing specifics discussed:
- Redwood Dedicated proposal: estimated commit $275k ARR (12-month reserved capacity) for target throughput (3000 RPS peak).
- Competitor offer (managed) came in at ~$95k ARR with lower SLO guarantees but acceptable latency in their benchmarks => procurement picked competitor.
- Net unit cost gap driven by per-token price and additional GPU premium for low-latency tails.

Technical notes / POC feedback:
- POC (Jan demo) showed 10–15% latency advantage on 2k token sequences; ops team said not worth premium.
- We proposed Optimize configs (quantization + batching) to lower unit cost by ~30% — customer concerned about model fidelity for clinical text.

Signals on deal health prior to close:
- Jan 08 demo, positive technical reception.
- Jan 20 security questionnaire submitted, no red flags but long legal review requested data residency SLA which increased risk.
- Feb 02 procurement asked for 2:1 price parity vs competitor; not achievable without deeper discounts or larger commit.

Why lost / stalled:
- No exec champion to push larger commit through finance.
- Procurement fixed on near-term OPEX savings; cannot absorb higher committed ARR even with performance gains.
- Competitive procurement play (aggressive pricing + quick onboarding) closed faster.

Follow-ups / next steps recommended:
- Close-out email sent 2026-02-11; record 'closed-lost' in CRM.
- Suggested 6–9 month nurture: monitor funding runway, product milestones (model fidelity improvements), re-open pricing conversation if usage profile or budget changes.
- Action: SE to prepare a short one-pager comparing real unit costs with and without Optimize recommendations for next re-engagement.
